sentences.text:
Learned counsel appearing for the parties submit that under the aegis of Mediation Centre, Saket Courts, New Delhi, the parties have been able to resolve their disputes and reduce the terms of settlement same into writing vide the Report dated 08.06.2023.
5.

According to the terms of settlement, petitioner no.1 is to remit to respondent no.2 a sum of Rs.5,80,000/- towards full and final settlement of all her claims, including maintenance (past,
present and future), permanent alimony, stridhan, mehar and iddat expenses, etc, in four equal instalments of Rs.1,45,000/-, each.
6.
Learned counsel for the petitioners jointly submit that a sum of Rs.4,35,000/- already stands paid in the interregnum.
Learned counsel appearing for respondent no.2 affirms the same.
In terms of the settlement, the remaining sum of Rs.1,45,000/- in the following manner:-
(i) Rs.1,25,000/- has been tendered to respondent no.2 by way of Demand Draft No.748602 dated 16.09.2023 drawn on Union Bank of India, Hariharpur, Lukhnow Branch.
(ii) A sum of Rs.20,000/- has been paid in cash, in Court, today.
7. Learned counsel for respondent no.2 affirms the aforesaid two payments.
8. The Mediation Settlement Agreement also notes that the parties have dissolved their marriage by way of divorce under the Muslim This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.
The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 20/10/2023 at 22:15:43 Shariya Law, by way of Talaq e Hasan, which is recorded in para 1 of the Settlement Agreement at page 34.
9. IO is present in person and identifies the parties who are present in Court.
10. This Court has interacted with respondent no.2, who affirms the terms of settlement.
She also confirms the receipt of Rs.5,80,000/- as full and final settlement and submits that she has no objection in case the aforesaid FIR is quashed.
11. This Court has perused the terms of settlement agreement and they appear to be lawful.
The parties are bound by the terms of the settlement.

12. After observing that the disputes are arising from matrimonial ties, this Court is of the considered opinion that no purpose would be served in continuing with the FIR in question and the further criminal proceedings and it would be in the interest of justice as also of the parties and the society that quietus is put to such disputes.
